newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Expansion work starts at main Ivory Coast airport.
newsitem.headline: Expansion work starts at main Ivory Coast airport.

text.p: The company running Ivory Coast's main airport has begun expansion work, designed to extend the runway and almost double the annual number of passengers handled to 1,700,000 within three years, officials say.
Felix Houphouet-Boigny international airport on the outskirts of the West African nation's commercial capital Abidjan handled 950,000 passengers in 1996.

Christian Rognone, managing director of AERIA (Aeoroport International Abidjan) told Reuters on Tuesday that the company would invest 16 billion CFA francs in the project, designed to expand the airport's role as a regional hub.
The runway would be extended from 2,700 to 3,000 metres to enable it to cater for fully loaded long haul flights, he said.

Rognone said the work began on Tuesday. Ivorian Prime Minister Daniel Kablan Duncan, who has toured the world to attract foreign investors to the world's top cocoa producer, launched the project at a ceremony on Monday.
The government gave AERIA the management of the airport for 15 years on July 1.
